clue.text: Hit back on item at back

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: back tells us to read the run of letters from the end, item followed by at turned round

parts.note: an item in a list is a detail

explanation.surface: Someone striking out at an item placed at the rear, perhaps in a stockroom squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit back' looks as though it might be the wordplay, but it is the definition; the single 'back' turns item and at together.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to respond in kind to an attack, so 'hit back' is a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Scratch handle turned in regular train

indicators.note: to scratch something is to strike it out, so letters are removed from the word regular
turned means the word for handle is read backwards before being struck out

parts.note: a lug is a handle or projecting ear on a pot

explanation.surface: Someone scratching a handle that was turned on a train that runs regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: LUG backwards is GUL, which sits in the middle of reGULar; strike it out and RE + AR remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children or animals is to bring them up, and to train them is part of that upbringing.

clue.text: Instruments we hear annoy ancient settlers

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are spoken, so we want what they sound like

parts.note: to try someone is to annoy them (try their patience), and the Angles were ancient settlers of England

explanation.surface: Musical instruments that irritate long-ago colonists.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY + ANGLES spoken aloud is the same as the name of the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a percussion instrument, a steel bar bent into three sides and struck with a beater.

clue.text: Metal in non-solid state on salver is deceiving

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the gas above the tray

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
gas is a state of matter that is not solid
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: A molten metal in a liquid state set on a serving dish appears deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading someone astray is misleading them, an idiom for deceiving or tempting them into error.

clue.text: Disconcerted Punch journalist supporting article

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below, so the punch and journalist go under the article

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
to bash is to punch
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A writer for the satirical magazine Punch is flustered while backing an article.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a long-running British humour magazine, which makes 'Punch journalist' look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means embarrassed or put out of countenance, so disconcerted is a close synonym.

clue.text: Cryptic crossword's primarily composition to occupy target

indicators.note: to occupy means to sit inside, so these letters are put inside the target word

parts.note: an end is an aim or target

indicators.note: primarily means first, so we take the opening letter of crossword's

parts.note: the first letter of crossword's
an ode is a poetic composition

explanation.surface: A crossword's main makeup aims at being cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something encoded is written in code, hidden in meaning, and so cryptic.

clue.text: Impressive ornate picture frames

indicators.note: frames means surrounds, so the answer is held within the words ornate picture

explanation.surface: An ornate frame makes a picture look impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective describes something grand or heroic in scale, hence impressive.

clue.text: Mates one put up in Hilton

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means moved higher, so the one is shifted one place earlier in the word

parts.note: Paris Hilton is the hotel heiress and celebrity
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Friends with one of them staying at a Hilton hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilton' reads as a hotel, but it stands for the heiress PARIS Hilton; moving the I up gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pairs are couples, and a mate is one of a pair, so mates matches as a plural noun.

clue.text: Teachers against, not for, people singing

indicators.note: not marks the swap: against appears in place of for

parts.note: professors are university teachers
pro means for
con means against

explanation.surface: Teachers who object to, rather than support, a group of singers.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap PRO in PROFESSORS for CON. 'Singing' is slang for confessing, informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing is underworld slang for owning up, so confessors are people who admit their guilt.

clue.text: A Muppet with a female name

parts.note: a muppet is British slang for a fool, as is a nit

explanation.surface: One of the Muppets puppets has been given a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Muppet, capitalised, suggests the puppets, but in British slang a muppet is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a common given name for a woman.

clue.text: Account by son involved in row about coming to office

indicators.note: involved in means put inside, so the son goes within the reversed row
about means turned round, so the word for row is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a loud noise

explanation.surface: An accountant's son caught up in an argument over someone taking up a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel or a line of seats, but here it is a din.
explanation.definitionFit: Accession is the attaining of a position, especially a monarch's taking the throne.

clue.text: Bold laundering money for American with external support

indicators.note: with external means the support goes round the outside of the other letters

parts.note: a sling is a support, as for an injured arm
laundering clothes is washing them
a buck is American slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A daring money-laundering scheme for an American, with outside backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Swashbuckling describes daring, flamboyant adventure, like a pirate hero, so it is a vivid synonym of bold.

clue.text: Moving hinged brackets close to me made beastly sound

indicators.note: brackets means encloses, so the rearranged letters hold the last letter of me
moving means the letters of hinged are shifted into a new arrangement
close to means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of me

explanation.surface: A creaking hinged door near someone sounded like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: HINGED rearranged as NEIGHD holds E (the end of 'me') to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To neigh is the cry a horse makes, so it is a sound uttered by a beast.

clue.text: Passage this writer will read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud means we want the sound of the contraction, which matches the answer

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, so this writer will becomes I'LL

explanation.surface: An author promising to recite a passage from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a piece of text but here means a walkway; I'LL said aloud gives AISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, such as in a church or plane.

clue.text: Scruffy lad served up jelly and cake

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means turned upside down, so the jelly is read backwards

parts.note: agar is a jelly made from seaweed
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A shabby boy brought jelly and cake to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a dirty, ragged child, typically a boy in torn clothes.

clue.text: Claimed part of body gets bitten by Welshman

indicators.note: gets bitten by means the other word closes around this one like jaws

parts.note: Aled is a typical Welsh man's name, as in the singer Aled Jones
the leg is a part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone asserted that a man from Wales had bitten their leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleged means asserted without proof, so it matches claimed as a past participle.

clue.text: Plants go by craft, taken to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the west means right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to sail is to travel by boat
had means taken, as in had a biscuit

explanation.surface: Flowers travelling by boat, carried off westward.
explanation.walkthrough: SAIL then HAD, all reversed, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are garden flowers with showy blooms, grown from tubers.

clue.text: Aim of busy environmentalist, saving marvels at sea

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters of environmentalist are bustling about into a new order
saving means except, so the letters of marvels are left out
at sea means confused, so the letters of marvels are taken out in any order

explanation.surface: The goal of an active green campaigner who rescues wonders of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M, A, R, V, E, L, S from ENVIRONMENTALIST, leaving E N I O N N T I T, which rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is what one plans to do, so it is a synonym for an aim or purpose.

clue.text: Pitches in Italian town cut by good person going round

indicators.note: cut means the town loses its final letter

parts.note: Assisi is a hill town in Umbria, Italy

indicators.note: going round means turned about, so the saint's letters are reversed

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Football pitches in an Italian town, interrupted by a holy man doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitches' looks like a noun but the definition is the verb phrase 'pitches in'; St Francis of Assisi makes the saint a natural fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in is to help out, which is what someone does when they assist.

clue.text: Slug oddly found on dirty bear

indicators.note: in a down clue, found on means sitting above, so the slug letters come first
oddly means take the first, third and so on letters of the word

parts.note: the odd letters of slug, first and third
to stain something is to dirty it

explanation.surface: A slug turns up, strangely, on a grubby teddy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' poses as an animal or toy, but it is the verb meaning to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a load or a loss is to bear it, an exact verb synonym.

clue.text: Cycling clubs release series of reports

indicators.note: cycling means letters go round from one end to the other, here the last to the front

parts.note: putters are golf clubs used on the green

explanation.surface: Cycling clubs publish a set of reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' looks like documents but means bangs; move the final S of PUTTERS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To sputter is to make a rapid run of small popping noises, as an engine misfires.

clue.text: Celebrity party hosted by Labour leader? I'm hesitant to go

indicators.note: hosted by means placed inside the other letters
to go means these letters leave the leader's name

parts.note: Keir Starmer is the leader of the UK Labour Party
er is the sound one makes when hesitant
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A star's party thrown by the head of the Labour Party, where a guest is reluctant to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: STARMER without ER is STARM, which takes in DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being famous, the condition of a celebrity.

clue.text: Brown book uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: Numbers is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A brown-bound book revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment giving a dark brown colour.

clue.text: Tight spot to accommodate large screen

indicators.note: to accommodate means to hold within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a bind is an awkward predicament
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A cramped space has to fit a big screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind is a window shade, something that screens a room from light or view.

clue.text: Relax being left in bed with space

indicators.note: in means the left letter goes inside the bed word

parts.note: sack is slang for bed, as in hit the sack
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Someone unwinding, left lying in bed with plenty of room.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure, half an em, used for spaces between words.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken is to loosen or ease off, so as a verb it means relax.

clue.text: Cat in this drop would be hurt

parts.note: put the word cat inside the answer, between its first two letters, and the result is a word meaning hurt

explanation.surface: A cat falling from here would be injured.
explanation.walkthrough: Put CAT between the first and second letters of the answer to get SCATHED, meaning harmed; the def 'drop' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something, like leaves or a skin, is to let it fall, a synonym of drop.

clue.text: Enchanting place announced cost to ride antelope

indicators.note: announced means we hear the words spoken, and their sound gives the answer

parts.note: a fare is a cost of travel and an eland is an African antelope; the fare goes on top of the eland, riding it

explanation.surface: Someone declares the price of an antelope ride.
explanation.walkthrough: FARE before ELAND, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairyland is the magical realm of fairies, an imaginary land full of enchantment.

clue.text: Language in which pupil's set first bit of homework

parts.note: the pupil of the eye is set in the middle of the iris

indicators.note: first bit of means just the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of homework

explanation.surface: A schoolchild sets about a language exercise with the first bit of homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' poses as a schoolchild, but it is the black centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish, or Irish Gaelic, is the Celtic tongue spoken in Ireland.

clue.text: After refusal, detective signals assent

indicators.note: After means the detective comes after the refusal

parts.note: no is a refusal
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: Having said no at first, a detective agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head is a gesture of agreement, so nods signals yes.

clue.text: Incredible mind a genius endlessly exercised

indicators.note: exercised suggests letters worked about and moved into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of genius is dropped

explanation.surface: An unbelievable mind of a genius, put through its paces endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: GENIUS loses its S, and MIND, A and GENIU are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unimagined is beyond what anyone has conceived, so it is unthinkable or incredible.
